title: Rung 1 -- coverage of one generated triangle against Cycles, no light model in the comparison

criterion.says: our own generated fixture -- rung 1 of the ten scenes: one triangle at about 30 % of the frame under a declared camera

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

camera.derivation: The framing rule of doc/requirements.md I.26.10 applied to this subject's own bounds: direction azimuth 35 deg and elevation 20 deg in glTF's +Y-up frame, distance r / sin(yfov/2) / 0.6 at r = 0.661437822678302 m, and yfov = 2*atan(12/50) from Blender's factory 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL. The roll is -arctan(1/2) = -26.5650511771 deg, derived rather than set: for an edge of irrational raster slope the perpendicular pixel-centre offsets equidistribute over +/-0.5 px, so the smallest margin over L boundary pixels is about 0.5/L and it SHRINKS as the subject grows -- measured between 2e-5 and 1.8e-3 px here, under the oracle's own 5e-3 px jitter. For a slope p/q in lowest terms the same distance is exactly 0.5/sqrt(p^2+q^2) at every pixel centre in the plane and does not depend on L at all, and tan(45deg+t) and tan(90deg+t) stay rational whenever tan t does, so a roll of rational tangent keeps a rational silhouette rational. The previous -22.5 deg maximised edge-to-AXIS angle, which is not the quantity the comparison turns on. The SIGN is the convention src/gltf/Subject.cpp states: a camera roll of +r turns the camera's right vector towards its up vector, so the image of the world rotates by -r. This subject's silhouette is not rational at any roll, so what the change buys it is a different draw of the same lottery and not exactness -- a property of the subject, and the reason its class is general-position.
camera.note: The generated subject carries no camera, so this rung's camera is declared here and the oracle builds the same one from these numbers.

light.note: A coverage rung compares a mask. The only illumination is Blender's factory world, which costs nothing to match and is left where it is.

world.note: Configured by not being configured. The observed colour and strength go into provenance.json, so a Blender that changed them is visible without any machinery that refuses.

material.note: Diffuse BSDF with Roughness pinned to 0, never Principled: Principled at metallic 0 still carries a specular lobe at IOR 1.5. This subject is a single unoccluded facet, which is the one shape where Cycles has no integration left and the answer is the closed form rho*L = 0.8 x 0.05087608844041824 = 0.0407008707523346 -- so this is one of the cases that keeps that number exercised (doc/requirements.md I.26.13).

default.note: The binary mask. One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does, because the integer raster coordinate is the pixel centre and the sample never leaves +/-0.005 px of it.

notes: Rung 1's subject is generated here rather than fetched (doc/requirements.md I.26.5 row 1), so a red at rung 1 has exactly one cause: every vertex is ours and none of them came from a file. It carries NORMAL as well as POSITION even though a coverage comparison reads neither, because the alternative -- admitting a normal-less vertex for one fixture -- is a shape change to the engine bought by a test.

subjectFrameFraction.derivation: the sum over the subject's triangles of the magnitude of the projected signed area, over 1280*720 at the declared camera, recomputed by the runner from the generated vertices
subjectFrameFraction.note: What the boundary bound is applied UNDER: I.26's IoU ~ 1 - P*d/A makes P/A a property of the subject's size, so a camera that framed the subject smaller would tighten the bound without saying so. The runner recomputes it from the generated vertices and refuses a mismatch. Every triangle is counted by the magnitude of its signed area, so a closed body counts its far side too and this is an AREA, not a coverage.
